subject: art-design
title: Drawing & Composition: Application
welcome_lead: Use perspective, leading lines and structural drawing to make believable, well-composed images.
meta_desc: Applying perspective, leading lines, gesture vs structural drawing for GCSE composition.
final_note: Apply these tools and even a quick sketch will feel intentional.

concepts.def: All depth lines converge on one vanishing point.
Depth lines converge to two vanishing points.
The viewer's eye level where vanishing points sit.
Lines that guide the eye towards a focal point.
Fast loose drawing capturing pose and movement.
Careful drawing using underlying shapes and forms.

walkthroughs.body_html: In 1-point perspective you look straight at a wall and all receding edges meet at one vanishing point — good for corridors. In 2-point perspective you view a corner and edges race off to two vanishing points on the horizon line — useful for buildings.
Roads, fences, arms and shadows can all act as leading lines, pulling the viewer's eye through the page towards the focal point. Diagonal leading lines feel more dynamic than horizontal ones.
Begin with a 30-second gesture drawing to feel the action, then layer structural drawing over the top — boxes, cylinders, ovals — to lock in proportion before adding tone or detail.
